items.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997
items.q: I still berate Dave Brubeck whenever I see him because he and Paul used to come in the club

ctx.x: Yeah. And I still berate Dave Brubeck whenever I see him because he and Paul used to come in the club and I would think oh isn’t that nice they really like the trio. But they were really coming in to size up Joe and steal him. But I mean Joe had to move on, he couldn’t stay with me forever. But anyway, thinking back, ten years of being in there was a good gig.
You had a lot of times — would you feel pressured when Duke Ellington came in the room, or — I mean I know you went out of your way to play some of his tunes and he apparently liked it.

items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Years later I was able to do that, recording with Dave Brubeck.

ctx.x: What were some of those technicalities that you mean?

Thinks like . . . [laughs] for instance I had this engineer. This is just one instance. Teddy [Wilson] and I made this record together, and . . . Wait a minute. Which one was it? No, I think it was in Argentina. Teddy made a horrible . . . played a really bad note. I said to this engineer—we were listening to everything—I said, “My God, let’s get rid of that for him. Let’s take that out.” It is so clever what they do. They take a little phrase from somewhere else. You probably know this. They had the same three…

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was playing at the Hickory House with Marian McPartland.

ctx.x: Tell me about Joe Morello coming into the quartet. How did that change things? And is it true that Paul Desmond was unhappy with that change in the band?

Paul Desmond asked me to go hear Joe Morello. He was playing at the Hickory House with Marian McPartland. We were at the Blue Note. So we went over there in our intermission. This marvelous drummer. He was playing brushes. Paul just loved somebody that played brushes and didn’t interrupt with some hard licks with sticks and clashing cymbals. So he said, as long as Joe Dodge has to go home to San Francisco, maybe this is the guy. So I talked to Joe. Joe was going to be on a vacation, because Marian McPartland was…
go live with Paul, when he was dying. They became so close to each other. Everybody in the group was close to each other. Eugene Wright was so wonderful all those years.
